items.section_heading: Basketball - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: List any five important rules of the basketball game.
items.answer: Five important rules of basketball are: (i) the duration of the game of each quarter is ten minutes, with 2 minutes rest between 1st and 2nd quarter and 3rd and 4th quarter and 15 minutes rest between 2nd and 3rd quarter; (ii) a team must consist of twelve (12) members, but only five players from each team may be on the court at one time, and substitutions are unlimited but can only be done when the play is stopped; (iii) the ball is moved in two ways, either dribbling or by passing to teammates, and if the ball goes out of the court the ball possession is given to the opposite team; (iv) two points are awarded when a basket is scored during the game but three points are awarded when a basket is scored from outside the 6.25 mtrs line; (v) each player is allowed 5 personal fouls before they are disqualified from the game. The game is controlled by three referees, one of whom is the overall incharge, with table officials keeping the records.
grounding: The duration of the game of each quarter is ten minutes with 2 minutes rest between 1st and 2nd quarter and 3rd and 4th quarter, also 15 minutes rest between 2nd and 3rd quarter.
A team must consist of twelve (12) members. But only five players from each team may be on the court at one time. Substitutions are unlimited but can only be done when the play is stopped.
The ball is moved in two ways: either dribbling or by passing to teammates. If the ball goes out of the court, the ball possession is given to the opposite team.
Two points are awarded when a basket is scored during the game but three points are awarded when a basket is scored from outside the 6.25 mtrs line.
Each player is allowed 5 personal fouls before they are disqualified from the game. At this point they no longer remain a part of the game.
The game is controlled by the officials consisting of the three (3) referees, out of which one (1) is the overall incharge and the other four (4) table officials

items.stem: List any five penalties of basketball game.
items.answer: The penalties given in the chapter are: (i) an attempt to unfairly disadvantage an opponent through physical contact is illegal and called a foul; (ii) players who are fouled get ball possession; (iii) or the fouled player is awarded one or two free throws; (iv) one point is awarded for successfully converting a free throw, which is attempted from a line 15 feet (4.6 m) from the basket; (v) each player is allowed 5 personal fouls before they are disqualified from the game, and at this point they no longer remain a part of the game. In addition, if the ball goes out of the court, the ball possession is given to the opposite team.

items.section_heading: Cricket - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: List the basic rules of the game of cricket.
items.answer: The basic rules of cricket given in the chapter are: (i) cricket is a game played between two teams consisting of eleven players each; (ii) there is also a reserve player called a twelfth man, who can only be utilized as fielder and who is not allowed to ball, bat, do wicket keeping or captain the team, his sole duty being to act as a substitute fielder; (iii) two umpires are placed on the playing field while there is also a third umpire off the field who is in charge of video decisions, and when the call is too close for the on field umpires they refer it to the third umpire, who reviews slow motion video replays to make a decision; (iv) the aim of the batsmen is to score runs, and a batsman hits a boundary and scores 4 or 6 runs -- if the ball crosses the boundary after touching the ground it is considered as four and if it crosses the boundary before touching the ground it is considered as six; (v) other ways runs can be scored include no balls, wide balls, byes and leg byes, and all runs scored by these methods are awarded to the batting team but not the individual batters; (vi) there are a number of different ways a batsman can be given out in the game of cricket.
grounding: Cricket is a game played between two teams consisting of eleven players each. There is also a reserve player called a twelfth man, who can only be utilized as fielder.
The twelfth man is not allowed to ball, bat, and wicket keeping or captain the team. His sole duty is to act as a substitute fielder.
Two umpires are placed on the playing field while there is also a third umpire off the field who is in charge of video decisions.
When the call is too close for the on field umpires then they refer it to the third umpire who reviews slow motion video replays to make a decision.
The aim of the batsmen is to score runs.
A batsman hits a boundary and scores 4 or 6 runs. A four and six both are scored by hitting the ball.
If it crosses the boundary after touching the ground it is considered as four and if the ball crosses boundary before touching the ground it is considered as six.

Other ways runs can be scored according to the cricket rules include no balls, wide balls, byes and leg byes. Cricket rules state that all runs scored by these methods are awarded to the batting team but not the individual batters.
There are a number of different ways a batsman can be given out in the game of cricket.

items.stem: What are the penalties that the Referee can award against offences during the match?
items.answer: If the player persistently offends during a match, the referee can choose to take action, and the penalties are: (i) the Yellow Card, shown first as a caution to the player; (ii) a Red card for any offence after the second one, which means that the player is expelled from the match; (iii) a straight red card with no previous caution for extreme offences such as serious foul play, violent conduct, spitting, deliberately handling the ball to prevent a goal, a professional foul (denying a goal scoring opportunity) and insulting language and/or gestures; (iv) a free kick, of which there are two types depending on the nature of the offence -- a Direct Free Kick, which allows the team to take a direct shot at the opponent's goal, and an Indirect Free Kick, in which a second player has to touch the ball after the kick is taken to score a goal; (v) a penalty kick, which is awarded for offences taking place in the penalty and goal areas and is struck at goal from the penalty spot by a nominated member of the team, with only the goalkeeper to beat.

items.section_heading: Football - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: What are the rules regarding free kick, penalty kick, throw-in and corner kick?
items.answer: Free kick: whenever a free kick is taken, the players on the opposite side must be at least 10 yards away from the ball until it is kicked, and if this rule is not adhered to the kick is retaken; there are two types depending on the nature of the offence -- a Direct Free Kick, which allows the team to take a direct shot at the opponent's goal, and an Indirect Free Kick, in which a second player has to touch the ball after the kick is taken to score a goal. Penalty kick: it is awarded for offences taking place in the penalty and goal areas; a nominated member of the team is allowed to strike at goal from the penalty spot with only the goalkeeper to beat, the goalkeeper must remain on his line until the ball has been kicked, all other players must be outside the penalty area behind the penalty spot, and after the kick that player cannot strike the ball again without another player touching the ball. Throw-in: it is awarded when the whole ball crosses the touch line, conceded by the team who last touched the ball; it is delivered on the field of play with both hands and from behind and over the player's head, and a goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in. Corner kick: it is awarded once the whole ball crosses the goal line of the opposition after touching one of their players; a kick is taken from the corner of whichever side the ball travelled over the field, opponents must be 10 yards from the corner arc, and the kicker cannot touch the ball a second time without having touched by any other player.

items.section_heading: Hockey - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: Write a brief note on the history of Hockey in India.
items.answer: The modern game of field hockey was developed in the British Isles in the 19th century, and it was introduced in India by the British Army regiments, after which the game soon became popular. It was during this time that the London Hockey Association was formed and the rules for playing hockey were standardised, and in 1924 the International Hockey Federation (FIH) was founded. In India, the first hockey club came up in Calcutta in 1885-86 and soon Bombay and Punjab followed. Making its Olympic debut at the 1928 Amsterdam Games, Indian hockey team won its first Olympic gold, without conceding a single goal. The hallmark of this ruthless domination was the wizardry of Indian hockey legend, Dhyan Chand, who mesmerised the Amsterdam crowd with his dazzling skills. From 1928 to 1956, India won six consecutive Olympic gold medals, while winning 24 consecutive matches. It was the golden era of Indian hockey, when India produced some of the finest players the game has ever seen.

items.section_heading: Hockey - I. Answer the following Questions
items.stem: What are the rules of the game in respect of (i) field, (ii) players, (iii) equipment, (iv) free hits, (v) long corner, (vi) short corner, and (vii) penalty stroke?
items.answer: (i) Field: hockey is played on a 91.40 m x 55 m rectangular field; at each end there is a goal 2.14 m high, 1.20 m deep and 3.66 m wide measured from the inner sides of the posts and crossbar, the goal post is surrounded by an approximately semi-circular area 14.63 m from the goal bounded by a solid line, and a spot 0.15 m in diameter, called the penalty spot, is marked with its centre 6.40 m from the centre of each goal. (ii) Players: field players may only play the ball with the flat side of the stick; tackling is permitted as long as the tackler does not make contact with the attacker or his stick before playing the ball, and the player with the ball may not deliberately use his body or stick to shield the ball from a legitimate tackle. (iii) Equipment: each player carries a stick, normally a little over 3 feet (90 centimeters) long and 2 inches wide, traditionally made of wood but now often made with fiberglass, Kevlar and carbon fiber composites, with a rounded handle flattening out on one side and with a hook at the bottom. (iv) Free hits: they are awarded when offences are committed outside the scoring circles, the ball may be hit or pushed once in any direction by the team offended against, and opponents must move 5 mt away from the ball. (v) Long corner: the chapter calls this a corner -- it is awarded if the ball goes over the backline after last being touched by a defender, and corners are played by the attacking team and involve a free hit from the 22.90 meter line. (vi) Short corner: this is the penalty corner, a set play awarded against a defending team when any offence is committed in the defensive circle, when a deliberate offence is committed in the defending 23 m area, or when the defending team deliberately plays the ball over the back line. (vii) Penalty stroke: it is awarded when defenders commit a deliberate foul in the circle which deprives an attacker of possession or the opportunity to play the ball; it is taken by a single attacker against the goalkeeper from a spot 6.4 m from the penalty spot and directly in front of the goal, and the goalkeeper must stand with heels on the goal line, and cannot move his feet until the ball is played.

items.stem: Three consecutive contacts with the ball made by the same team are allowed.
items.answer: True. The rally continues, with each team allowed up to three consecutive touches; it is four consecutive contacts with the ball made by the same team that is a fault.
grounding: The rally continues, with each team allowed up to three consecutive touches

items.answer: False. Two consecutive contacts with the ball made by the same player is listed among the common faults of volleyball.

items.stem: The player touches the net during play.
items.answer: False. Touching the net during play is listed among the common faults, and when a team commits a fault and loses the rally the point goes to the other team.
